speaker: Unknown
en: Thinking for yourself sounds both simple and trivial, but in reality, it's extremely difficult and it's profound.
zh: 独立思考听起来既简单又微不足道，但在现实中，它极其困难且深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's why.
zh: 原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: As human beings, we want to be liked.
zh: 作为人类，我们想要被人喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's anthropological.
zh: 这是人类学层面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If people didn't like you in caveman days, they would just eat you.
zh: 如果在穴居时代人们不喜欢你，他们就会直接把你吃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you really have a natural built-in instinct to want to be liked.
zh: 所以你真的有一种天生的本能，想要被人喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the easiest way to be liked is to tell people what they want to hear.
zh: 而被人喜欢的最简单方法就是告诉人们他们想听的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know what everybody wants to hear?
zh: 你知道每个人想听的是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What they already believe to be true.
zh: 他们已经确信为真的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the last thing they want to hear is an original idea that contradicts their belief system.
zh: 所以他们最不想听到的就是一个与他们信念体系相悖的原创想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very hard to even bring that kind of stuff up.
zh: 所以甚至很难把这类事情提出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But those are the things, those are the only things, things that you believe
zh: 但正是这些事情，这些唯一的事情，你相信的事情

speaker: Unknown
en: That everybody around you doesn't believe, when you're right, that create real value in the world.
zh: 你周围每个人都不相信的事情，当你是对的时候，那些是在世界上创造真正价值的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Follow your passion may be the most common piece of career advice graduates receive.
zh: “追随你的激情”可能是毕业生收到的最常见的职业建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ben Horowitz disagrees.
zh: Ben Horowitz 不同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this commencement address to Columbia University's Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science, Ben argues that passion is often a byproduct of mastery, contribution, and achievement, not necessarily the starting point.
zh: 在这次给哥伦比亚大学 Fu Foundation 工程与应用科学学院的毕业典礼演讲中，Ben 认为激情往往是精通、贡献和成就的副产品，不一定是起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Drawing on his own experiences as a student, entrepreneur, investor, and technologist, he shares lessons on independent thinking, conviction, innovation, and why some of the most valuable opportunities come from pursuing ideas that other people don't yet believe.
zh: 借鉴他作为学生、企业家、投资者和技术专家的自身经历，他分享了关于独立思考、信念、创新的教训，以及为什么一些最有价值的机会来自于追求其他人还不相信的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, thank you so much.
zh: 谢谢，非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a beautiful speech.
zh: 那是一场精彩的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very nice work.
zh: 非常出色的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna take my hat off if that's okay with you guys, because I don't want to get too excited and have it spill.
zh: 如果你们各位不介意的话，我要把帽子摘下来了，因为我不想太兴奋然后把它弄掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even though it is an awesome hat.
zh: 虽然这是一顶很棒的帽子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first of all, thank you, class of 2015, for inviting me to speak.
zh: 所以首先，谢谢你们，2015 届的毕业生，邀请我来演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's such a great honor.
zh: 这是莫大的荣誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I got the invitation, I started thinking back to when I was in Columbia.
zh: 当我收到邀请时，我开始回想我在哥伦比亚大学的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember getting to Columbia and I was immediately super stressed out because I realized that I now had to figure out at some point what I was gonna do with my life.
zh: 记得来到哥伦比亚大学，我当时立刻超级有压力，因为我意识到我现在必须在某个时刻搞清楚我这辈子要做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was like super scary.
zh: 那非常可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of you might be going through that now a little bit.
zh: 你们中有些人现在可能正在经历一点这种情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: But not to bring that up or anything.
zh: 但我并不是要提起这个或者别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember when I kind of first got the first clue of what I might do, I was taking a class over in the Mudd building, which somebody was telling me today.
zh: 记得当我第一次得到关于我可能会做什么的线索时，我正在 Mudd 大楼上课，今天有人告诉了我这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somebody was telling me today, Mudd is great if you like prisons and Catholic school.
zh: 今天有人告诉我，如果你喜欢监狱和天主教学校，Mudd 是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was in this class and they were talking about this guy, Alan Turing, and they were talking about how he had proven
zh: 我当时就在那个班上，他们在谈论这个人，Alan Turing，他们在谈论他是如何证明

speaker: Unknown
en: That if you built a machine that was what he called a Turing machine, that it was theoretically impossible to build a machine that was computationally more powerful.
zh: 如果你建造了一台他称之为图灵机器的机器，那么从理论上讲，不可能建造出一台计算能力更强的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, it just like melted my mind when I heard it because I couldn't even imagine like what he was talking about because it was 1984.
zh: 我当时就像，听到的时候它简直让我大脑融化了，因为我甚至无法想象他在谈论什么，因为那是 1984 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to remember in 1984, computers weren't even really a thing.
zh: 而且你要记得，在 1984 年，计算机甚至还不算是真正存在的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the idea of like a machine that could do anything was just like so far fetched because all of our machines were like these special purpose machines.
zh: 所以关于一台可以做任何事情的机器的想法，简直就是太牵强了，因为我们所有的机器都是这些专用机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we had a special purpose machine for doing math.
zh: 比如我们要么有一台用于做数学的专用机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your parents will remember it was called a calculator.
zh: 你们的父母会记得它被称为计算器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we had one for word processing called a typewriter.
zh: 然后我们要么有一台用于文字处理的，叫做打字机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we even had one for video called a television set.
zh: 我们甚至有一台用于视频的，叫做电视机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the idea of like, okay, now you're going to have a machine that can do absolutely anything.
zh: 所以像这样的想法，好吧，现在你将拥有一台可以做绝对任何事情机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this guy had figured that out 40 years ago and I didn't even know about it.
zh: 而这人在 40 年前就搞清楚了，而我甚至都不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I had no idea.
zh: 就像我完全不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like the secret to the universe, which they were just saying, oh, here, oh, by the way, there's a machine that's like limitless and you can do anything on it.
zh: 这就像宇宙的秘密，而他们只是在说，噢，这里，顺便说一句，有一台机器是无限制的，你可以在上面做任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just like, no way.
zh: 我当时就想，没门。

speaker: Unknown
en: Translate Español No Way Jose.
zh: 翻译成西班牙语就是“No Way Jose”。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the parents, that's a Kanye West reference.
zh: 对于在座的父母来说，这是引用 Kanye West 的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was kind of at that point in my life where it was like, for those of you who are Phineas and Ferb fans, it was like that time when Phineas goes, I know what I'm gonna do today.
zh: 但这就像是我生命中那个时刻，对于那些 Phineas and Ferb 的粉丝来说，这就像 Phineas 说的那个时刻，“我知道我今天要做什么了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna major in computer science.
zh: 我要主修计算机科学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I ran over to Carmen,
zh: 所以我跑到了 Carmen，

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just so excited to tell my friends.
zh: 而我当时只是太兴奋了，想告诉我朋友们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, man, they're going to be just so fired up for me.
zh: 我当时想，伙计，他们肯定会为我感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I figured it out.
zh: 我弄明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not going to be stressed anymore.
zh: 我再也不会有压力了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, guys, I'm going to major in computer science.
zh: 我就说，伙计们，我要主修计算机科学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of my friends said, wow, that's the stupidest thing I've ever heard.
zh: 我的一个朋友说，哇，那是我听说过的最愚蠢的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, why?
zh: 我说，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, you're at Columbia University.
zh: 他说，你在哥伦比亚大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like a trade.
zh: 那就像是一种手艺。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can learn that at DeVry.
zh: 你可以在 DeVry 学到那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll teach you how to build computers, fix them, program them.
zh: 他们会教你如何组装电脑，修理它们，给它们编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should major in something real.
zh: 你应该主修一些真正的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just thinking to myself, I was like, I'm talking about a limitless machine.
zh: 而我只是自己在想，我当时想，我在谈论的是一台无限的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like talking about a washing machine.
zh: 你却在谈论一台洗衣机。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was so frustrated, I couldn't even really explain to him why.
zh: 但我是如此沮丧，我甚至无法真正向他解释原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was at that point, at my height of frustration, that I learned the most valuable lesson that I learned at Columbia, which is don't listen to your friends.
zh: 但就在那一刻，在我沮丧的顶点，我学到了我在哥伦比亚学到的最有价值的一课，那就是不要听你朋友的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the more generalized case of don't listen to your friends is think for yourself.
zh: 而“不要听你朋友的”更普遍的情况就是独立思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And thinking for yourself sounds both simple and trivial, but in reality, it's extremely difficult and it's profound.
zh: 独立思考听起来既简单又琐碎，但实际上，它极其困难且深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's why.
zh: 原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: As human beings, we want to be liked.
zh: 作为人类，我们想要被喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's anthropological.
zh: 这是人类学上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If people didn't like you in caveman days, they would just eat you.
zh: 如果在穴居时代人们不喜欢你，他们就会直接吃掉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you really have a natural built-in instinct to want to be liked.
zh: 所以你真的有一种天然的内在本能想要被喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the easiest way to be liked is to tell people what they want to hear.
zh: 而被喜欢的最简单方法就是告诉人们他们想听的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know what everybody wants to hear?
zh: 你知道每个人想听什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What they already believe to be true.
zh: 他们已经认为是真的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the last thing they want to hear is an original idea that contradicts their belief system.
zh: 所以他们最不想听到的就是一个与他们信念体系相悖的原创想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very hard to even bring that kind of stuff up.
zh: 所以甚至很难把这类事情提出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But those are the things, those are the only things, things that you believe
zh: 但那些事情，那是唯一的事情，那些你相信的事情

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I see this in my business every day.
zh: 而我每天在我的生意中都能看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my business is I fund people who have companies.
zh: 所以我的生意是，我资助那些拥有公司的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you, like some of you, probably have company ideas, and you might come to me and say, I've got an idea.
zh: 所以如果你们，你们中的有些人，可能有创业想法，你可能会来对我说，我有个主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the biggest thing that I'll look for when you come to me with an idea is, have you thought for yourself, is it something that you know that nobody else knows, or is it something that everybody knows?
zh: 而当你带着一个主意来找我时，我最看重的一点是，你是否独立思考了，这是你知道的别人都不知道的事情，还是大家都知道的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll give you an example.
zh: 我给你们举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, if you came to me and said, hey, I've got an idea to make batteries and cell phones last longer, I would go, well, that's a pretty good idea, but I'm not going to fund it because everybody thinks that's a good idea.
zh: 举个例子，如果你来对我说，嘿，我有个主意能让电池和手机续航更久，我会说，好吧，那是个好主意，但我不会资助它，因为每个人都认为那是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because everybody thinks that's a good idea, companies like Google and Apple and Samsung with tons of resources will just build that.
zh: 而且因为每个人都认为那是个好主意，像 Google 和 Apple 和 Samsung 这样拥有大量资源的公司只会直接把它造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not really a new value creation for like a new person.
zh: 所以这并不是真正为一个新人创造的新价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you contrast that with an idea that came to me about five years ago.
zh: 你可以把这个和一个大约五年前来到我这里的想法对比一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: A young man by the name of Brian Chesky came up to me, and he had this idea that he was going to have an air mattress in his apartment that he rented to people, and it was going to be like an air bed and breakfast.
zh: 一个名叫 Brian Chesky 的年轻人来到我面前，他有个主意，他要在他的公寓里放一个充气床垫租给别人，这就好比是一个充气床早餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, that's a horrible, horrible idea.
zh: 我当时想，哇，那是一个极其糟糕的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because who would want to rent an air mattress out of somebody's apartment like probably a serial killer?
zh: 因为谁会想从某人的公寓里租一个充气床垫，很可能是个连环杀手？

speaker: Unknown
en: But Brian had a secret, and his secret was, one, he had run the experiment, he had actually tried it, and a whole lot of people wanted to rent that air mattress, and they weren't serial killers.
zh: 但 Brian 有一个秘密，他的秘密是，第一，他做了实验，他实际上试过了，而且很多人想租那个充气床垫，而且他们不是连环杀手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then beyond that, once he did that, he went and he studied kind of the history of hotel chains and he found that hotel chains were a relatively new concept.
zh: 然后除此之外，一旦他那样做了，他去研究了酒店连锁的历史，发现酒店连锁是一个相对较新的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that before hotel chains, people stayed at inns and bed and breakfasts.
zh: 在酒店连锁之前，人们住在旅馆和家庭旅馆里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that the problem with inns and bed and breakfasts were they were like a box of chocolates.
zh: 旅馆和家庭旅馆的问题在于它们就像一盒巧克力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had no idea what you were gonna get.
zh: 你不知道你会得到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, you know, one day you might have like something good and the other day you might have marzipan cherry or some weird stuff.
zh: 就像，你知道，有一天你可能会有不错的东西，另一天你可能会得到杏仁糖樱桃或者一些奇怪的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he thought, wow, with the internet, we can make every one of those little chocolates in the box transparent and you can know what you're getting.
zh: 所以他想，哇，有了互联网，我们可以让盒子里的每一颗小巧克力都透明化，你可以知道你会得到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you'd get all like the greatness of the bed and breakfast and all the goodness of the hotel chain all in one.
zh: 然后你就能一次性获得家庭旅馆的所有伟大之处和酒店连锁的所有优点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he had figured out that secret.
zh: 所以他发现了那个秘密。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was an interesting secret because it was something that probably everybody in the world knew at one point, but they had all forgotten.
zh: 这是一个有趣的秘密，因为它可能是世界上每个人在某个时刻都知道的事情，但它们都忘记了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody had forgot why we had hotels.
zh: 每个人都忘记了我们为什么要有酒店。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that ended up being, now I think they rent more nights every night in New York than Hilton Hotel, just five years ago, and it was all based on him believing something that nobody else believed.
zh: 结果这变成了，现在我认为他们在纽约每晚租出的晚数比希尔顿酒店还多，就在仅仅五年前，而且这都是基于他相信了别人不相信的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in that spirit, what I'd like to give is a few unconventional graduation thoughts, and I'm titling them...
zh: 本着这种精神，我想给出一些非传统的毕业典礼思考，我将它们命名为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Do not follow your passion and the world is not going to hell in a handbasket and the class of 2015 is not required to save it.
zh: 不要追随你的热情，世界并不是在一手提篮里走向地狱，2015 届毕业生也不被要求拯救它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I told you it was going to be unconventional.
zh: 我告诉过你，这将是非传统的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't follow your passion.
zh: 所以不要追随你的热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you're probably thinking, that's a really dumb idea.
zh: 现在你可能在想，这真是个愚蠢的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because everybody who's successful, and if you, Paul, a thousand people are successful, they'll all say that they love what they do.
zh: 因为每个成功的人，如果你，Paul，一千个人是成功的，他们都会说他们热爱他们所做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the broad conclusion of the world is that if you do what you love, then you'll be successful.
zh: 所以世界上的广泛结论是，如果你做你爱做的事，你就会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're engineers, and we know that that might be true.
zh: 但我们是工程师，我们知道那可能是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it also might be the case that if you're successful, you love what you do.
zh: 但也可能是因为如果你成功了，你就会热爱你所做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just love being successful, and everybody loves you, it's awesome.
zh: 你只是热爱成功的感觉，每个人都爱你，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So which one is it?
zh: 那么是哪一种呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think to figure it out, you kind of have to go back in time.
zh: 嗯，我认为要弄清楚这一点，你还得回到过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to back off when you were successful to like right now when you're graduating as the class of 2015.
zh: 你得从你成功的时候退回到就像现在你作为 2015 届毕业生毕业的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first tricky thing about passions are they're hard to prioritize.
zh: 关于热情的第一件棘手的事情是，它们很难排优先级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which passion is it?
zh: 是哪一种热情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you more passionate about math or engineering?
zh: 你对数学还是工程更热情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you more passionate about history or literature?
zh: 你对历史还是文学更热情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you more passionate about video games or K-pop?
zh: 你对电子游戏还是 K-pop 更热情？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are tough decisions.
zh: 这些都是艰难的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you even know?
zh: 你怎么甚至知道？

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, what are you good at?
zh: 另一方面，你擅长什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you better at math or writing?
zh: 你是更擅长数学还是写作？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a much easier thing to figure out.
zh: 那是一件容易弄清楚得多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing that's tricky if you're going forward in time with this follow your passion idea is that what you're passionate about at 21 is not necessarily what you're gonna be passionate about at 40.
zh: 如果你带着这个追随热情的想法向前看，第二件棘手的事情是，你在 21 岁时充满热情的事情不一定是你在 40 岁时还会充满热情的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now this is true for boyfriends as well as career choices.
zh: 现在这对于男朋友和职业选择来说都是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third issue with following your passion is, excuse me, a little trouble with the throat, is you're not necessarily good at your passion.
zh: 追随热情的第三个问题是，抱歉，喉咙有点不舒服，是你不一定擅长你的热情所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And has anybody ever watched American Idol?
zh: 有人看过《美国偶像》吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you know what I'm talking about.
zh: 所以你知道我在说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like just because you love singing doesn't mean you should be a professional singer.
zh: 就像仅仅因为你热爱唱歌并不意味着你应该成为一名专业歌手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally and most importantly, following your passion is a very me-centered view of the world.
zh: 然后最后也是最重要的是，追随你的热情是一种非常以我为中心的世界观。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you go through life, what you'll find is what you take out of the world over time, be it whatever money, cars, stuff, accolades, is much less important than what you put into the world.
zh: 当你度过一生时，你会发现你从世界上拿走的东西，无论是金钱、汽车、物品、荣誉，都不如你给予世界的重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my recommendation would be follow your contribution.
zh: 所以我的建议是追随你的贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find the thing that you're great at, put that into the world, contribute to others, help the world be better, and that is the thing to follow.
zh: 找到你擅长的事情，把它奉献给世界，贡献给他人，帮助世界变得更好，这才是值得追随的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of the world, so this is generally the point in a graduation speech where I should say the class of 2015 faces unprecedented challenges.
zh: 说到世界，所以这通常是毕业演讲中我应该提到 2015 届毕业生面临前所未有挑战的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's ISIS, there's global warming.
zh: 有 ISIS，有全球变暖。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sucks.
zh: 这很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't get me started on congressional gridlock.
zh: 别让我提国会僵局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think all those things are true, but what's remarkable from a historical standpoint about this time in the world to me are not the unprecedented challenges,
zh: 我认为所有那些事情都是真的，但从历史角度来看，对我来说，关于当今世界这个时期值得注意的并不是前所未有的挑战，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the unprecedented opportunities.
zh: 而是前所未有的机遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let me just kind of talk quickly about the state of the world.
zh: 让我只是快速谈谈世界状况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the number of people living in extreme poverty today is the lowest in the history of the world and one fifth of what it was in 1900.
zh: 所以今天生活在极端贫困中的人数是世界历史上最低的，是 1900 年时的五分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Child labor is in steep decline and fell one third between 2000 and 2012.
zh: 童工数量急剧下降，在 2000 年到 2012 年间下降了三分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compared to the late 19th century, the number of hours that one has to work has fallen roughly in half.
zh: 与 19 世纪末相比，一个人必须工作的时间大约减少了一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: The percent of income spent on food has fallen in half since 1960.
zh: 自 1960 年以来，用于食物的收入百分比下降了一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life expectancy has increased six years between 1990 and 2012.
zh: 预期寿命在 1990 年到 2012 年间增加了 6 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Child mortality has fallen in half since 1990.
zh: 儿童死亡率自 1990 年以来下降了一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are getting taller, which is a measure of nutrition.
zh: 人们正在长高，这是营养的一个衡量标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have grown more in the last 100 years than in the previous 2000.
zh: 在过去 100 年里，人们的生长比之前的 2000 年还要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of ISIS, worldwide battlefield deaths are down 20-fold since the 40s.
zh: 说到 ISIS，自 40 年代以来，全球战场死亡人数下降了 20 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: The homicide rate in the US is down half since the late 70s.
zh: 自 70 年代末以来，美国的凶杀率下降了一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Violent crime is one-third of what it was in 1976.
zh: 暴力犯罪是 1976 年时的三分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: The global supply of nuclear weapons is down nearly five-fold since 1990.
zh: 自 1990 年以来，全球核武供应量下降了近五倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 2014 was the first year in 40 that carbon emissions were flat.
zh: 2014 年是 40 年来碳排放量持平的第一年。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not that bad.
zh: 所以情况没那么糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the biggest opportunity is one that we've only begun to measure.
zh: 但最大的机会是我们才开始衡量的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to explain this, I'd like to go back to when your parents and I were in college.
zh: 为了解释这一点，我想回到你父母和我读大学的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when we were in college, and they may have told you this, and it may have scared you, so I apologize for scaring you, but we didn't have the internet.
zh: 因为当我们读大学时，他们可能告诉过你这一点，这可能吓到你了，所以我为吓到你而道歉，但我们当时没有互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no internet.
zh: 没有互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if we had an idea, like Brian Chesky had an idea and we wanted to find out about it, we couldn't Google it.
zh: 所以如果我们有一个想法，就像 Brian Chesky 有一个想法，我们想了解它，我们无法 Google 它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we did have a search engine.
zh: 但我们确实有一个搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a different kind of technology.
zh: 这是一种不同类型的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was called a library.
zh: 它被称为图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it kind of sucked.
zh: 而且它有点烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's actually an old search engine behind me.
zh: 实际上我身后有一个旧的搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm looking at it there.
zh: 我正在那里看着它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of sucked because, one, you couldn't access it from your dorm room because it wasn't even in cyberspace.
zh: 它有点烂，因为第一，你无法从宿舍房间访问它，因为它甚至不在赛博空间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was in actual space.
zh: 它是在现实空间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you had to walk over there.
zh: 你必须走到那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you had to bring your credentials or they wouldn't even let you in.
zh: 然后你必须带上你的凭证，否则他们甚至不会让你进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no logged out user experience.
zh: 没有未登录的用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it was based on this really weird tech that was invented a long time ago called the Dewey Decimal System.
zh: 然后它是基于很久以前发明的一种非常奇怪的技术，叫做杜威十进制分类系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this tech was so old, like Dewey was named after the guy Dewey who invented it.
zh: 而且这项技术太老了，就像 Dewey 是以发明它的那个人 Dewey 命名的一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to make it seem high tech, they said it's like a decimal system.
zh: 但为了让它看起来很高科技，他们说这就像是一个十进制系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this is so high tech, we're using numbers, dude.
zh: 就像，这是如此高科技，我们在用数字呢，伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not just integers.
zh: 而且不仅仅是整数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got decimals up in that bar.
zh: 在那个条目里还有小数呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the user interface to it was so bad it was called a card catalog.
zh: 然后它的用户界面太糟糕了，它被称为卡片目录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was so bad they had to train you to use it.
zh: 它太糟糕了，他们不得不训练你才能使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You couldn't just go in and use it.
zh: 你不能直接进去使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You needed hours and hours of classroom training.
zh: 你需要数小时的课堂训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the net result of this was that looking stuff up was very discouraging because you couldn't look it up in milliseconds.
zh: 因此，这样做的最终结果是，查找东西非常令人沮丧，因为你无法在几毫秒内查到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took hours.
zh: 它需要几个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's if you were a Columbia student and you had a good library like Butler.
zh: 而且这还是如果你是哥伦比亚大学的学生，并且你有一个像 Butler 那样好的图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would take you hours to look things up.
zh: 查找东西会花费你几个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was very discouraging.
zh: 所以这非常令人沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe if Brian Chesky was born, then he would never have, like, even, he would have just said, like, forget this, I'm going to Taco Bell.
zh: 你知道，也许如果 Brian Chesky 出生了，他永远不会，就像，甚至，他只会说，就像，算了吧，我要去 Taco Bell。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not figuring out where hotels came from.
zh: 我不去弄清楚酒店是哪里来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But think about it.
zh: 但想一想。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's for a Columbia student.
zh: 那还是针对哥伦比亚大学学生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even worse for, like, a student who didn't go to Columbia and didn't have access to as good a library and, you know, might not even have that book in the library.
zh: 对于，比如，一个没去哥伦比亚大学的学生来说，情况更糟，没有渠道使用那么好的图书馆，而且，你知道，图书馆里甚至可能没有那本书。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or even more so, imagine you grew up in Bangladesh or Sudan and you had all kinds of great ideas.
zh: 或者甚至更甚，想象一下你在孟加拉国或苏丹长大，你有着各种各样很棒的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had no access, no search engine at all, no way to contribute your original ideas to the world.
zh: 你没有任何渠道，根本没有搜索引擎，无法为世界贡献你的原创想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we fast forward to where we are now.
zh: 然后我们快进到我们现在的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everybody who has a smartphone, which is pretty soon gonna be everybody in the world, has the Library of Congress in their pocket.
zh: 每个拥有智能手机的人，这很快将是世界上的每个人，口袋里都有国会图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that means a girl growing up in Bangladesh now has a better library than a student at Columbia or Harvard had 20 years ago.
zh: 所以这意味着一个现在在孟加拉国长大的女孩拥有一个比 20 年前哥伦比亚大学或哈佛大学的学生拥有的更好的图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what might her idea be?
zh: 那么她的想法可能是什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What might she contribute?
zh: 她可能会做出什么贡献？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that's gonna be a lot up to you because the world still isn't flat.
zh: 嗯，我认为这在很大程度上取决于你，因为世界仍然不是平的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are issues.
zh: 存在问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are issues with power and issues with water and issues with food and issues with equal rights.
zh: 有能源问题，有水资源问题，有食物问题，还有平等权利的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you contribute, if you put your contribution into the world, if you think for yourself, then I believe that you will be the greatest generation.
zh: 但是如果你做出贡献，如果你把你的贡献付诸世界，如果你独立思考，那么我相信你们将是最伟大的一代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when we look back 50 years from now, 100 years from now, 500 years from now, you will be the generation that unlocked human potential.
zh: 因为当我们在 50 年后、100 年后、500 年后回顾时，你们将是解锁了人类潜能的一代。

speaker: Unknown
en: So congratulations, Columbia Class of 2015, and thank you for inviting me.
zh: 所以祝贺你们，哥伦比亚大学 2015 届，并感谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening to this episode of the A16Z podcast.
zh: 感谢收听这一期的 A16Z 播客。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果你喜欢这一期，请务必点赞、评论、订阅，给我们打分或评论，并与你的朋友和家人分享。

zh: 更多内容请前往 YouTube、Apple Podcasts 和 Spotify。

zh: 在 X 上关注我们 @A16Z，并在 a16z.substack.com 订阅我们的 Substack。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks again for listening, and I'll see you in the next episode.
zh: 再次感谢收听，我们下一期再见。
